## Poike Peninsula excursion: eastern Easter Island

The [Poike Peninsula](/chile/place/poike-peninsula/) lies in the east of [Easter Island](/chile/place/easter-island/). Open grassy slopes meet the ocean, and rocky shores remind visitors that beyond the archaeological complexes, Rapa Nui is also a volcanic island with remarkable natural scenery.

We include Poike on a **full-day excursion to archaeological sites and the coast**. This product does not offer a separate extended trek across the peninsula or an ascent of all its hills.

## Which excursion does Ada Tours offer?

[“Anakena, Rano Raraku and Ahu Tongariki”](/chile/easter-island/anakena-rano-raraku-tongariki-tour/) is a full-day excursion stopping at sites that reveal different aspects of Rapa Nui culture.

The itinerary starts at [Ahu Akahanga](/chile/place/ahu-akahanga/), which local tradition associates with the island's first king, Hotu Matu'a. Travelers continue to [Rano Raraku volcano](/chile/place/rano-raraku-volcano/), the famous quarry where moai statues were carved from stone. Unfinished figures remain on its slopes.

A **packed lunch**, included in the program, follows this section. The next stop is [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/), a ceremonial platform with **15 restored moai**.

The route then continues to the **Poike Peninsula** and [Ahu Te Pito Kura](/chile/place/ahu-te-pito-kura/). The day ends at [Anakena Beach](/chile/place/anakena-beach/), with white sand and palm trees, before guests return to Hanga Roa.

## What a visit to Poike adds

After the quarry and ceremonial platforms, the peninsula offers a more open landscape. Attention shifts from individual stone structures to the coastline, grassy slopes and ocean views.

This is an opportunity to discover the island's geography. However, the itinerary is built around **several different attractions**, so do not assume you will spend hours walking on Poike. Discuss the exact stop and the available walking section in advance.

## How this route differs from a visit devoted only to moai

The sites on the itinerary illustrate different periods and aspects of local history:

- Rano Raraku is where stone statues were carved.
- Ahu Tongariki is a restored ceremonial platform.
- Poike reveals the natural setting of the eastern coastline.
- Anakena offers beach scenery to close the excursion day.

This combination of archaeology, ocean views and coast differentiates the trip from a visit to one monument. Set aside separate time for detailed exploration of a quarry or a long walking route on Poike.

Rapa Nui's archaeological monuments are protected. Follow permitted visiting routes and your local guide's instructions. Do not approach moai too closely or cross barriers for photographs.

## Preparing for the excursion

This is a full-day trip. Bring comfortable footwear, sun protection, a hat and water for the road; coastal weather and wind can change quickly. A packed lunch is provided, but other services and restrictions should be checked on the [excursion page](/chile/easter-island/anakena-rano-raraku-tongariki-tour/).

The island has specific access rules for archaeological sites, which should be checked for your visit date. A site appearing on the itinerary does not grant unrestricted access to every part of the protected area.

## Frequently asked questions about the Poike Peninsula

### Is Poike a separate excursion or part of a longer route?

In the Ada Tours catalog, Poike is included in the full-day [Anakena–Rano Raraku–Ahu Tongariki itinerary](/chile/easter-island/anakena-rano-raraku-tongariki-tour/).

### Is an ascent of the Poike Peninsula included in the price?

A separate ascent or extended trek is not listed in the published description. The confirmed activity is a visit to the peninsula area as part of the excursion day.

### How many moai can you see at Ahu Tongariki?

The restored [Ahu Tongariki](/chile/place/ahu-tongariki/) platform has 15 moai. Other statues can be found at Rano Raraku and other archaeological sites.

### Is lunch included?

A **packed lunch** is included in the excursion. A full restaurant lunch is not separately promised.

## Torres del Paine in one day: Mylodon Cave, lakes and waterfalls

**This trip reveals several of Chilean Patagonia's famous landscapes in a single day.** Our route starts near [Puerto Natales](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/), includes Mylodon Cave and viewpoints overlooking the mountains and lakes of Torres del Paine National Park, then continues via Pehoé Lake and Salto Grande waterfall.

The excursion is **private and lasts a full day**. Admission fees and lunch at a local restaurant are included. The exact sequence of stops and drives depends on weather and arrangements for your chosen date.

This is a way to discover the national park without undertaking the difficult multi-day W or O trails. The focus is on viewpoints and the changes in landscape from open steppe to glacial lakes.

## Mylodon Cave: a prehistoric animal's story

The first part visits [Mylodon Cave](/chile/place/mylodon-cave/) on Cerro Benítez. Remains of a giant extinct ground sloth that once lived in prehistoric South America were discovered here.

The cave is significant for geology, paleontology and the history of the region's first inhabitants. Chile's official monuments register lists it among natural and archaeological sites linked to Patagonia's ancient history.

This is more than a brief photographic stop. The visit helps explain why the remains of a large animal were preserved within a limestone and rocky setting, how the cave itself is structured and what it reveals about environmental changes in southern South America.

## Lakes Sofía, Porteño and Toro on the way to the park

After the cave, the route passes viewpoints around Lake Sofía, the Prat Range and lakes Porteño and Toro. These stops show a broader, calmer Patagonian landscape before entering the high mountain area.

On clear days, the ridgelines and water are visible across long distances; low cloud may hide some peaks. Photographic opportunities depend heavily on weather, and the operator may adjust the order of viewpoints.

Scenery along the road is part of the experience. Visitors seeking to understand Patagonia's varied landscapes do not need to make a strenuous ascent every day: a scenic excursion reveals transitions between valleys, mountains and lakes.

## Grey Glacier and a walk through lenga forest

One main part of the excursion is [Grey Lake](/chile/place/lake-grey/) and the surrounding area. The route includes views from Mirador Grey, panoramas of the water and floating icebergs, and **a walk through lenga forest to the shore**.

Grey Glacier belongs to the glacier system of the Southern Patagonian Ice Field. Ice masses and floating fragments may create striking contrasts with dark water and mountain slopes. The number of visible icebergs and conditions at viewpoints, however, are constantly changing.

Distinguish this stop from a separate glacier cruise or extended hike toward the ice. This excursion includes land-based views of the lake and a walk to the shore; a separate boat embarkation is not listed in its program.

## Pehoé, Salto Grande and Lake Nordenskjöld

In the second part of the day, the route visits [Pehoé Lake](/chile/place/lake-pehoe/), [Salto Grande waterfall](/chile/place/salto-grande-waterfall/) and the area around Lake Nordenskjöld, followed by Laguna Amarga.

Pehoé is particularly known for the turquoise colors of its water and mountain views. Salto Grande connects lake systems with a powerful flow, illustrating how glacial rivers shape the landscape. The stops differ: the lake provides distant mountain panoramas, while the waterfall offers a close view of moving water.

| Stop | Main experience |
|---|---|
| Mylodon Cave | Patagonia's prehistoric history |
| Grey Lake | Glacial scenery and icebergs |
| Pehoé | Mountain panoramas across the water |
| Salto Grande | Powerful water flow |
| Laguna Amarga | Open park landscapes |

**Lunch at a local restaurant** is included. Its timing depends on the route; special menus and additional drinks are not separately confirmed.

## Planning for a full-day outing

Patagonian weather changes quickly: strong winds, rain, cold and sunshine may follow one another within hours. Waterproof and windproof outerwear, closed shoes and several layers of clothing are useful.

The excursion combines scenic driving stops with walking sections. Even without strenuous trekking, check whether viewpoints are accessible to you and whether you can comfortably walk over uneven ground.

The national park administration determines access rules, temporary closures and visitor behavior requirements. Compare inclusions with the actual tour: **admission fees and lunch are confirmed**, but extra lake cruises or separate trekking routes are not automatically included.

Find other nature trips in our [nature and wildlife section](/interests/wildlife/).

## Frequently asked questions about Torres del Paine

### Can you see Torres del Paine in a day?

Yes. This full-day excursion introduces several of the park's signature natural sites. It does not replace multi-day walking routes deeper into the park.

### Is Mylodon Cave included?

Yes. Mylodon Cave is the first confirmed stop on the itinerary.

### Is lunch included?

Yes. Ada Tours specifies **lunch at a local restaurant and admission fees**.

### Will there be a boat ride to Grey Glacier?

The confirmed program lists views of Grey Lake, icebergs and a walk through lenga forest to the shore. It does not list a separate glacier cruise.

## Tours featuring a private Torres del Paine excursion

Chilean Patagonia is remarkable for the varied landscapes that can be seen in one day: mountain ranges, broad lakes, glacial waters and windswept valleys. The [private Torres del Paine excursion](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/chile-torres-del-paine-private-full-day/) combines a visit to **Mylodon Cave** with national park viewpoints. It is a **full-day** experience, with **admission fees and restaurant lunch included**.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} featuring this exact excursion. It is part of the [“Chile and Argentina: 17-Day Grand Tour with Iguazu in Brazil”](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/) on **day eight**. The following day, travelers leave Chilean Patagonia for El Calafate in Argentina.

## What happens during the excursion day?

The first major stop is **Mylodon Cave** near Cerro Benítez. Remains of the extinct giant ground sloth were discovered here, connecting natural scenery with the region's geological and paleontological history.

The route then passes views of **Lake Sofía**, the Prat Range, **lakes Porteño and Toro**, and the **Mirador Grey** area. From the lookout, travelers see Grey Lake and floating icebergs. The itinerary provides a walk through lenga forest to the shore and lunch at a local restaurant.

The second part of the day covers **Pehoé Lake**, **Salto Grande waterfall**, Lake Nordenskjöld and **Laguna Amarga**. This is a scenic drive with stops and some walking, not a lengthy athletic trek to the Torres towers simply because both options share the park's name.

## How the excursion fits into the 17-day Grand Tour

The [17-day journey](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/) links several regions of South America: Chilean cities and nature, Easter Island, the Atacama, Patagonia, then Argentina and Iguazu. Day 8 is specifically devoted to Torres del Paine National Park. The itinerary includes admission, lunch and an overnight stay at **The Singular Patagonia, Singular Room**, with **BB breakfast**.

Travel continues the next day to El Calafate, Argentina. It is important to distinguish the nature excursion day from the subsequent international transfer. Headwinds, weather and road conditions may affect walking pace, so departure times and the precise stop sequence are coordinated for the selected trip.

An **optional helicopter flight** over the park's glaciers and peaks may be arranged separately for **$800–1200 per hour**. It is an additional activity and is not part of the private sightseeing excursion featuring Mylodon Cave, lakes and waterfalls.

## How the Grey Glacier boat excursion differs

| Program | Main way of seeing the park |
|---|---|
| [Private day in the park](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/chile-torres-del-paine-private-full-day/) | Viewpoints and walks |
| [Boat to Grey Glacier](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/grey-glacier-boat-paine-full-day/) | Sailing toward the ice wall |

Both independent excursion products operate in Torres del Paine and may mention Grey Lake and Mylodon Cave, but they are **different itineraries**. The 17-day Grand Tour specifically includes the private route with land viewpoints and lenga forest. The separate [Grey Glacier boat excursion](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/grey-glacier-boat-paine-full-day/) focuses on sailing across the water. Shared lake names do not mean the boat is automatically included on the private sightseeing day.

This difference is especially important if the glacier is your main reason for traveling. Choose the product that includes your preferred method of visiting and confirm its availability for the selected date.

## Frequently asked questions about tours featuring private Torres del Paine

### On which day does the park excursion take place?

On the [17-day Grand Tour](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/), it is scheduled for **day eight**.

### What is included in the excursion price?

**Admission fees and lunch** are included. The program lasts a full day.

### Is there a boat trip to Grey Glacier?

Boat navigation is not included in the confirmed private sightseeing program. A separate [boat excursion](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/grey-glacier-boat-paine-full-day/) is available.

### Is the helicopter flight included?

No. The Grand Tour lists it as an **optional** experience costing **$800–1200 per hour**.

### Where do travelers stay after the park visit?

On the 17-day tour, the night after Torres del Paine is at **The Singular Patagonia**, in a Singular Room, with breakfast.

## Grey Glacier and the lakes of Torres del Paine in one day

The centerpiece of this excursion is [Grey Glacier](/chile/place/grey-glacier/) and its towering wall of ice above the lake. The journey continues to natural attractions of Torres del Paine National Park and ends with [Mylodon Cave](/chile/place/mylodon-cave/).

This is an activity-packed **full day**. It combines sailing with a sightseeing route through the national park, unlike a short outing that stops at just a few lakes.

## Sailing to Grey Glacier

The first major experience is **a boat journey toward Grey Glacier**. From the water, travelers can appreciate the height and colors of its ice formations, and the contrast between the broad glacier and floating ice fragments. How close the vessel can sail depends on weather, wind and water conditions.

[Grey Lake](/chile/place/lake-grey/) lies among mountain landscapes associated with the glacial system of southern Patagonia. On cloudy days, ice floes can stand out dramatically against the dark water. The captain and current safety rules determine the permitted approach to the glacier front; boats cannot simply sail any desired distance from the ice.

**The boat trip to the glacier is included**, an important distinction from excursions that offer sailing as a separately paid option.

## Lakes, cliffs and Salto Grande waterfall

After returning to the pier, the itinerary continues through several natural stops. It lists Lake Sofía, the Prat mountain massif, Lake Porteño, Cerro Mesa and Lake Toro. These show the diversity of Chilean Patagonian landscapes on the way to the Paine massif.

There is then a viewpoint overlooking **Pehoé Lake** and **Salto Grande waterfall**, approximately **18 meters high**. The combination of rushing water, rocky shores and distant mountains is particularly striking here.

The route continues to Lake Nordenskjöld, Laguna Amarga and Lake Sarmiento. Different lakes can appear different colors because of depth, light and natural particles. The purpose of the journey is to compare several parts of the national park rather than concentrate on a single famous summit.

## Mylodon Cave and ancient Patagonia

Alongside glaciers and lakes, the excursion includes **Mylodon Cave**, a paleontological site associated with the discovery of prehistoric animal remains. It adds the story of changes to local fauna and climate to the natural scenery.

The cave is a meaningful stop in its own right: after experiencing today's mountain ecosystems, travelers learn about animals that once inhabited this region.

The cave lies in the Puerto Natales area. Its inclusion is confirmed, although the order of stops may vary according to the boat schedule and travel time.

## What is actually included?

The excursion includes:

- **Admission tickets** to Torres del Paine National Park.
- **A boat journey** to Grey Glacier.
- **Lunch** during the excursion day.

No separate price is stated for this excursion. Prices of other trips in the park do not apply to it. Transfer arrangements, guiding language and exact start time should be confirmed when booking.

## Weather and safety

Strong winds, rain and falling temperatures are possible around the glacier and at exposed viewpoints. Even in summer, bring a warm jacket, waterproof clothing and shoes with good grip on wet surfaces. Follow crew instructions on the vessel; weather restrictions may affect sailing.

The excursion's demands arise from its full-day duration, weather and potential walks between viewpoints, rather than mountain climbing. An extended trek to the Torres towers is not included in its description.

Compare this product with the [group Torres del Paine sightseeing excursion](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/torres-del-paine-national-park-group-tour/): **the Grey Glacier boat trip and Mylodon Cave are confirmed on this route**, whereas the shorter group tour has different stops. Other options appear in the [Chile tours catalog](/chile/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about Grey Glacier

### Is the boat to the glacier included?

Yes. It is expressly listed among Ada Tours' included services.

### Is lunch provided?

Yes. Lunch is included together with national park admission tickets.

### Which lakes are visited?

The itinerary lists Sofía, Porteño, Toro, Pehoé, Nordenskjöld, Amarga and Sarmiento. Exact stops depend on current road and weather conditions.

### Does the route include Mylodon Cave?

Yes. It is one of the stops.

## Tours including a boat excursion to Grey Glacier

[Grey Glacier](/chile/place/grey-glacier/) lies in Chilean Patagonia and is famous for its blue wall of ice seen from the water. [“Torres del Paine and Grey Glacier: Boat, Lakes and Mylodon”](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/grey-glacier-boat-paine-full-day/) is a full-day excursion whose main feature is sailing toward the glacier. It includes **national park admission, the boat journey and lunch**.

Our selection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} featuring this exact program. It is part of [“VIP Chile 5*”](/chile/tour/chile-five-star-vip/): **day 7** is devoted to Torres del Paine, Grey Glacier and Mylodon Cave. Unlike transfers between cities, this part of the tour is entirely focused on the nature of southern Chile.

## How the glacier visit unfolds

The program begins with **a boat journey toward Grey Glacier**. From the water, travelers see its ice wall and surrounding mountains. After returning to the pier, the itinerary explores Torres del Paine National Park: Lake Sofía, the Prat Range, Lake Porteño, Cerro Mesa and Lake Toro, followed by views of **Pehoé Lake** and **Salto Grande waterfall**.

Additional stops include **Lake Nordenskjöld**, **Laguna Amarga**, **Lake Sarmiento** and Mylodon Cave. One day thus combines glacial scenery with other natural landscapes of Patagonia. The return to the hotel is scheduled for the evening.

The standalone excursion page confirms park admission, **the boat to the glacier** and lunch. Do not add a hike to the Torres towers, independent kayaking or landing on the glacier itself: these are not services in this product. The permitted approach to the ice front depends on navigation conditions and safety restrictions on the travel date.

## When is the glacier visited on VIP Chile 5*?

The [“VIP Chile 5*” tour](/chile/tour/chile-five-star-vip/) lasts **10 days**. It covers Santiago and Atacama, followed by Chilean Patagonia. On day six, travelers fly from Santiago to **Puerto Natales** and check into a hotel. On day seven, they travel through Torres del Paine, taking the boat toward Grey Glacier, having lunch and visiting Mylodon Cave. Day eight is devoted to the return journey from Puerto Natales to Santiago.

This sequence keeps the lengthy nature excursion separate from arrival day and allows a dedicated day for departure. Nevertheless, the boat section requires coordination of departure times, transport to the pier and sailing availability. Local conditions may affect the schedule, so the precise time at the glacier cannot be inferred from the tour title alone.

Patagonian weather changes rapidly. Pack warm windproof clothing, rain protection and comfortable closed-toe shoes for stops near the lakes. Follow operator instructions aboard the boat. A defining feature of the itinerary is its combination of **viewing the glacier from the water** and visiting natural attractions on shore.

## Grey Glacier boat or private park sightseeing?

| Excursion | Distinguishing feature |
|---|---|
| [Grey Glacier by boat](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/grey-glacier-boat-paine-full-day/) | Sailing toward the ice wall |
| [Private park sightseeing](/chile/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/chile-torres-del-paine-private-full-day/) | Lakes, viewpoints and forest walk |

These two products share some geographical stops, including lakes, a waterfall and Mylodon Cave. The confirmed difference is significant: **boat navigation is included only on the itinerary where it is expressly listed among the services**. The [17-day Chile and Argentina Grand Tour](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/) uses the separate private sightseeing excursion with land-based views of Grey Lake, whereas [“VIP Chile 5*”](/chile/tour/chile-five-star-vip/) includes the boat excursion.

If the glacier is your main travel objective, compare not just photographs and descriptions of the park, but also the actual excursion type, boat boarding arrangements and time available for other stops.

## Frequently asked questions about Grey Glacier tours

### Is sailing to the glacier included?

Yes. The excursion includes **a boat trip to Grey Glacier**, national park admission and lunch.

### Which day is the excursion on VIP Chile?

**Day seven**, after arrival in Puerto Natales. On day eight, travelers return to Santiago.

### Can you see the glacier from the shore instead?

A different private route in Torres del Paine visits viewpoints around Grey Lake. On this product, however, **the boat is central**; changing the format must be agreed separately.

### Is Mylodon Cave included?

Yes. It is one of the stops on the full-day route, along with lakes and viewpoints.

### Is landing on the glacier included?

No. Confirmed services cover sailing **toward the glacier**, not a separate landing or walk on the ice.
